title: Sunil Kumar Srivastava v. State of U.P.
court: High Court of Judicature at Allahabad
coram: Amreshwar Pratap Sahi, J. and Vivek Kumar Birla, J.
disposition: Writ disposed; consider Clause 4.4 application within six weeks.
headnote: A tenant supplied through the landlady's sub-meter, after she sought permanent disconnection, was relegated to Clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, including an indemnity bond. The Court did not mandamus a connection; it directed the licensee to consider the application and pass an appropriate order within six weeks.
facts: The petitioner, a tenant, had been supplied electricity through a sub-meter from the landlady's connection. The landlady had left for Kolkata and applied for permanent disconnection, leaving him without supply. He sought a writ for independent connection. Counsel for the Electricity Department stated that the claim would be considered if he completed the formalities under Clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, including an indemnity bond.

holding_units.holding: Where a tenant seeks independent supply after the landlady applies for permanent disconnection, the licensee is to consider the occupant's application under Clause 4.4 of the Electricity Supply Code, 2005, including an indemnity bond, and pass an appropriate order; the Court does not itself grant the connection.

not_decided.point: Entitlement of the tenant to a new connection on merits
not_decided.note: The Court directed consideration of the Clause 4.4 application; it did not decide whether a connection must be granted.
